result:
The proposed reasoning holds up, so the answer r/(r+1) appears correct.

**Upper bound.** Stars a+V fully inside T_X are indexed by a in T_{X/P}, and their count is C = Ψ_S(X/P) = (1+o(1))N, since the leading term of Ψ_S(X) is (log X)^r/(r! ∏ log p_i). Any set B hitting every such star must satisfy (r+1)|B| ≥ C, because each point lies in at most r+1 stars. So |A| ≤ (r/(r+1) + o(1))N.

**Lower bound.** Let φ(a) = Σ i·a_i mod (r+1). Since φ(0)=0 and φ(e_i)=i, V maps bijectively onto Z/(r+1). Every translate a+V therefore contains exactly one point with φ≡0, so the set {φ≠0} contains no forbidden configuration. The φ≡0 class is one coset of an index-(r+1) sublattice, and lattice-point counting in the dilating simplex gives it N/(r+1) + O((log X)^{r-1}) points. Hence |A| = (r/(r+1) + o(1))N.

**Checks.** For r=1 the formula gives 1/2, which matches the 2-colouring of chains {n, pn}. For S={2,3}, the colouring a+2b mod 3 gives density 2/3, consistent with the stated formula.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
CONFIDENCE: 4
